problem_description: Compute the average temperature in K, pressure in bar, and density in kg/m^3 of the guanidinium chloride solution in water. The system contained 32 guanidinium (GND) molecules, 32 chloride ions (CL-), and 230 water molecules (spc)in a cubic simulation box of dimensions 2.2 × 2.2 × 2.2 nm³ and was modeled using the gromos45a3 force field. Energy minimization was performed using the steepest descent algorithm for 100000 steps with an energy minimization step size of 0.002 nm using the Verlet cutoff scheme with neighbor list updates every step (nstlist = 1). Long-range electrostatic interactions were calculated using the Particle Mesh Ewald (PME) method with a real-space cutoff of 1.0 nm, while van der Waals interactions were truncated at 1.0 nm. Molecular dynamics simulations were performed using the md integrator with a time step of 0.002 ps and neighbor list updates every 10 steps. All bonds involving hydrogen atoms were constrained using the LINCS algorithm. The system was equilibrated in the NPT ensemble using the V-rescale thermostat and the Parrinello–Rahman barostat before the production simulation. The equilibration run should be run for 100 ps, and the production run for 200 ps using the same parameter as equilibration runs. Periodic boundary conditions were applied in the xyz directions. During the equilibration and production runs, the system compressibility was set to 4.5e-5 bar^-1, the temperature should be set to 300 K (with tau_p = 0.1 ps), and the pressure should be set to 1.0 bar (with tau_p = 2.0 ps).
